about.title: Perris Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death in Perris comes without warning, the questions arrive faster than anyone is ready for. Six people died in traffic collisions here in 2025, according to public records, and each of those numbers stands for a family now sorting through funeral arrangements, bills, and an empty place at the table. Wrongful death is the civil claim California gives those families. It is separate from any criminal case, and it exists so that a spouse, domestic partner, or child can seek recovery for burial costs, the income that will no longer arrive, and the loss of the person's love, companionship, and guidance. Some of the collisions that lead here happen on Perris Boulevard or 4th Street; others on the Ramona Expressway heading in or out of town. Wherever it occurred, we handle wrongful death cases in Riverside County. We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing, placing a spouse or domestic partner and children first, with certain dependents and heirs able to step in only in specific situations. We can sort out where your family fits before anything else moves forward.

items.title: Deadlines Explained Early
items.desc: Most wrongful death actions in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is much shorter when a city, county, or state agency may share responsibility. Knowing which timeline applies to your case is one of the first things we will address.

items.title: The Full Scope of Loss Considered
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. We work to account for each of these rather than only the receipts.

items.question: My spouse was killed in a crash on the Ramona Expressway. Does it matter who maintains that road?
items.answer: It can matter a great deal. If a public agency is potentially responsible for a roadway condition, California requires a formal claim on a much shorter timeline than the standard two-year wrongful death deadline. Our team is familiar with Riverside County claims and can determine whether a government entity is involved and what filing dates apply. Reaching out sooner rather than later keeps those options open.

items.question: Can I bring a wrongful death claim if the driver is also facing criminal charges?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death case is a civil action and proceeds separately from any criminal prosecution. The criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while the civil claim focuses on your family's losses. Neither one depends on the outcome of the other, although evidence from one can sometimes be useful in the other.

items.question: What does it cost to get started?
items.answer: Your initial consultation is free. We handle wrongful death cases in the Perris area on a contingency basis, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery.
